claims.claim: Simple Criterion conditions accept only the Arazzo 1.1 literals and operators.
claims.reason: The canonical Pest grammar and evaluator now enforce the Arazzo 1.1 literal/operator surface, including rejection of contains, matches and in. The specification requires case-insensitive string comparisons and failed evaluation for syntax/context/runtime errors, recommends reporting those errors, and recommends numeric-string coercion. The implemented error makes the owning condition false and is reported through the detailed/runtime criterion result; ordinary Step failure routing and later eligible Actions remain possible, so this is not a global no-side-effects guarantee. Maintainer-selected rules settle otherwise underspecified precedence, operand boundaries, strict boolean/null truth, missing-versus-present access, deterministic structural comparisons, and Unicode-lowercase text comparison. The accepted interpretation of the conflicting null prose/example makes every comparison with exactly one null or missing operand false, including !=; null == null is true, null != null is false, and !(value == null) is the existence spelling. Numeric support is deliberately bounded to existing i64/u64/finite-f64 storage: plain integer condition literals and numeric strings without a fraction or exponent must fit [-2^63, 2^64-1] without float fallback; fraction/exponent conversion rejects overflow and nonzero underflow to zero. Integers and mixed integer/represented-float values compare without rounding the integer to f64; represented floats use no epsilon and signed zero compares equal. Existing JSON/YAML loader rounding is unchanged and cannot be recovered; admitted decimal values may already coincide, so no end-to-end decimal exactness or typed JSONPath/XPath precision is claimed. Numeric-string coercion is adopted for all six comparisons only when exactly one operand is numeric and the other is a string fully matching JSON-number syntax without whitespace; invalid spelling/range fails evaluation. Two strings remain Unicode-lowercase text, deliberately declining that part of the SHOULD to avoid content-dependent string ordering. This aggregate boundary remains deviation for its bounded numeric support and partial SHOULD adoption, rather than covered or uniformly failClosed; the local null-clarification draft records the unresolved specification contradiction without claiming upstream resolution.

claims.claim: JSONPath Criterion and Selector expressions execute under RFC 9535 semantics when the version is omitted or rfc9535; any other declared JSONPath version and any syntactically invalid expression are rejected before evaluation (a criterion fails with an error, a selector resolves null with one warning).
retryAfter accepts decimal seconds and simple string comparisons are case insensitive.
